title: Heteroresistance and mixed infection
dek: A 8% rpoB minority, two lineages in one BAM, a cavity evolving under HPMZ. Filters, probes, and MGIT each have a different lower limit. Frequency is a clinical variable.
story: Heteroresistance: more than one resistance genotype in what we treat as one infection. Mixed infection: more than one strain (often different lineages) in one host. They overlap in a BAM and they are not the same epidemiological object. Unlinked lineage SNPs at 40/60 split say mixed infection; a single rpoB S450L at 8% on an otherwise clonal background says emerging RR.

Xpert needs enough mutant template to drop a probe. MGIT CC can grow the susceptible majority. WGS default filters at 10% will hide 8%. tNGS at 2000× will see 8% and also see PCR error if you do not have UMIs or replicates.
Clinical translation: a minority RR allele in a still-smear-positive patient is a rifampin problem, not an average of assays. Do not “vote” Xpert S vs NGS R vs MGIT S and pick the modal letter.
deep: Binomial: 2/20 reads is compatible with error; 80/1000 is not the same 8%. Depth is the denominator of DST.
Cavities are structured populations. Serial sputum is a drain sample, not a census of all lesions.
Microevolution vs mixed infection changes contact investigation (one source vs two).
Pipeline methods sections that omit AF thresholds are incomplete DST methods.

formulas.label: Allele fraction
formulas.expression: AF = mutant reads / depth at site
formulas.note: Report AF with DP. 0.08 at DP 20 ≠ 0.08 at DP 2000.

visual.caption: Schematic allele-fraction observations. Error/noise hugs zero. True emerging minorities sit at a few percent to tens of percent. Fixed resistance sits near one. Your filter is a vertical cut on this axis.

example.title: Two lineages, one rpoB
example.setup: L2 55% / L4 45% unlinked SNPs. rpoB S450L at 52%, sitting on L2-linked reads. L4 rpoB WT.

steps.title: This is mixed infection, not 50% microevolution
steps.body: Unlinked genome-wide split is the tell.

steps.title: RR is in the L2 population
steps.body: The patient still has RR-TB because one of the strains is RR. Do not treat the L4 DS clone and ignore the L2.

steps.title: Infection control and epi
steps.body: Two strains may mean two sources. Do not draw a single transmission arrow.

example.takeaway: Split the BAM into strain and resistance. Treat the worse DST.

choices: Heteroresistance is multiple resistance genotypes in an infection; mixed infection is multiple strains, which may also differ in DST
Mixed infection means NTM + TB only
check.answer: Heteroresistance is multiple resistance genotypes in an infection; mixed infection is multiple strains, which may also differ in DST

check.prompt: AF 0.10 at DP 20 versus AF 0.10 at DP 2000. The minority call is stronger in which?
choices: DP 2000, because binomial sampling/error is far less likely to produce ~200 mutant reads
They are identical in all statistical senses
check.answer: DP 2000, because binomial sampling/error is far less likely to produce ~200 mutant reads

whyWrong.DP 20, because 10% exceeds 5%: Percent without N is not enough.

seq error at 0.015 only as a fixed allele
